question: A neck swelling that moves upward with swallowing but does NOT move on tongue protrusion is consistent with a thyroid origin.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is actually true. A thyroid swelling moves on swallowing (pretracheal fascial attachment) but NOT on tongue protrusion. A thyroglossal cyst also moves on swallowing AND on tongue protrusion — that distinction separates the two.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Movement on swallowing is the hallmark of a thyroid swelling (the gland is enclosed in the pretracheal fascia, which is attached to the larynx). A thyroglossal cyst also moves on swallowing but additionally moves on tongue protrusion — because it is connected to the base of the tongue via the thyroglossal duct tract.
